idle.title: Nothing selected.

overview.oldTle: This element set is {d} days from the simulation time. SGP4 errors grow quickly with age, so treat positions as rough.

passes.title: Next 48 hours
passes.noneIn48h: No passes above the elevation mask in the next 48 hours.
passes.visibleHint: Sunlit in a dark sky: the satellite is in sunlight while your sky is dark. Whether you can see it depends on its size and brightness.
passes.skyplotLegend: Centre is straight up, the rim is the horizon. Circle: rise, square: set.
passes.note: Times are from SGP4 with the current TLE, refined to half a second. Atmospheric refraction is ignored, so very low passes rise a little earlier in reality. * started before the window.

doppler.note: Uses the satellite's velocity relative to the rotating Earth. First-order Doppler; relativistic terms are below 1 Hz at these frequencies.
doppler.title: Doppler
doppler.noFrequency: No known frequency for this object. Enter one to see the shift.

elements.title: Mean elements
elements.note: These are SGP4 mean elements, not osculating ones. They only make sense fed back into SGP4.

lifetime.title: Orbital lifetime
lifetime.dragUnknown: The drag term in this TLE is zero or too small to use, so lifetime can't be estimated from it.
lifetime.note: Rough estimate from the TLE drag term and a static exponential atmosphere. Real decay depends on the solar cycle, attitude and manoeuvres; manoeuvring satellites such as the ISS or Starlink won't come down on this schedule.
lifetime.manoeuvres: This object raises its orbit with thrusters, so drag alone doesn't decide when it comes down. The estimate assumes it stops manoeuvring.

conj.runningHint: Propagating every object whose orbit can come close. This can take a few seconds.
conj.idle: Checks the loaded catalog for objects that pass close to this one.
conj.none: Nothing comes within {km} km in the next {h} hours.
conj.note: A TLE-based screen, not a collision assessment. TLE positions can be off by a kilometre or more, so a small miss distance here is a reason to look, not a prediction.
conj.title: Close approaches

about.title: About
about.what: OrbitView propagates the public satellite catalog with SGP4 in your browser and draws it on a 3D globe. Select an object to see its passes over you, Doppler shift, elements, a lifetime estimate and close approaches.
about.accuracy: Accuracy is that of the TLEs: about a kilometre for a fresh LEO element set, getting worse by a few kilometres per day of age. Good for planning an observation or pointing an antenna, not for operations.
about.srcTle: Orbits: CelesTrak GP data (Space-Track when configured)
about.srcWeather: Solar flux and Kp: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
about.author: Built by Mehmet Gümüş. MIT licence, source on GitHub:

about.modelCredit: ISS 3D model: NASA 3D Resources (International Space Station (B), NASA/Michael D. Carbajal).

errors.computation: The calculation failed. Try another object or time.
errors.noTle: No element set for this object.
errors.globeBody: The 3D view stopped with an error. The rest of the app still works; reloading usually fixes it.
errors.noWebgl: This browser or device doesn't provide WebGL, which the 3D globe needs. Try a current Chrome, Firefox or Safari, or turn on hardware acceleration.

orbit.title: Orbit
orbit.frameNote: TEME is the frame SGP4 works in (Earth-centred, inertial). ECEF turns with the Earth. Values at simulation time.

tonight.title: Tonight
tonight.about: Passes of the ~100 brightest satellites (CelesTrak's visual list) that you can see with the naked eye from your location during the coming night: the satellite is in sunlight while your sky is dark. Times use the elevation mask set in Settings.
tonight.noNight: The Sun doesn't get far enough below your horizon in the next day and a half, so nothing will be visible.
tonight.none: No visible passes of bright satellites tonight.
